correctness.rationale: For fixed R>0, the disk Toeplitz spectrum is an exact incomplete-gamma integral with top gap Re^{-R}. A positive compact operator remainder at each center has mutually vanishing translated cross products, bounding the total remainder by ell_1+o(1). For coherent states at separated centers the alien-disk mass is <=R exp(-(d-sqrt R)^2); positivity bounds the off-block coupling by the square root of this quantity, and Schur reduction gives eigenvalue error O(exp(-(d-sqrt R)^2)). The 3x3 coherent Gram matrix is circulant with product phase sqrt(3)d^2/2, diagonalized by the cubic Fourier transform. Rotation symmetry decomposes the entire operator into three character sectors, in each of which a unique high eigenvalue continuously follows the cosine branch; reversal of the sector order establishes actual double crossings near each integer and half-integer flux. No step relies on numerical extrapolation. The independent finite-section quadrature checker passed 32 assertions.

value.rationale: A natural three-aperture Gaussian concentration problem has three high eigenvalues whose exponentially small splitting depends on gauge-invariant triangle area. Unlike two disks, this geometry admits a non-removable loop phase and infinitely many exact double degeneracies protected by separate rotation characters, with the other spectrum bounded away by a fixed disk gap. This is a sharp mechanism for mode competition and concentration near-degeneracies, rather than a routine restatement of disk extremality or of the classical coherent-state geometric phase.
